narrative_purpose: The dim full-bleed atmospheric backdrop the chapter's text floats over: ancient wind-carved stone arches of the Pandoran highlands receding into haze under a dark sky, evoking deep time and erosion, deliberately low-contrast so overlaid text stays readable.
subject: A vast field of ancient, weathered rock arches and eroded stone formations stretching to a low horizon, their surfaces worn smooth by hundreds of millions of years of wind. Most are dark silhouettes; a few catch a faint cool rim of light along their upper edges. Threads of dim bioluminescent teal trace a few crevices low to the ground. A pale sliver of a gas giant's curve sits dim and distant on the horizon.
scene: A wide panoramic highland vista from a high, far vantage at deep twilight, immense atmospheric haze layering the distance, almost everything dissolving into murk - mood, not a figure to study.
camera: Ultra-wide panoramic vista from a very high distant vantage, horizon low in the frame, great depth of layered haze.
light: Very dark and low-contrast; a faint cool rim along the tops of the nearest arches, a dim teal glow in low crevices, deep indigo shadow everywhere else; no bright focal light.
palette: Dominant void-indigo and deep teal-indigo, desaturated stone-grey silhouettes, a faint cyan haze low on the horizon; overall dim.
style: Painterly atmospheric vista, soft, dark, immersive; detail dissolving into haze.
detail_level: Low and soft throughout - deliberately dim and hazy so long-form text can float over it and stay legible.
composition: Low horizon; dark eroded arches receding across the frame; wide empty hazy sky above; nothing bright competing for attention.
consistency_notes: Same cool Pandora palette and any gas giant must match Polyphemus elsewhere. Must stay dark and low-contrast as a background layer, distinct from the crisp bright cover.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no bright focal point, no high contrast, no sharp foreground, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
